task.description: Validate the fix design at src/design/fix-ISS-0106.md for ISS-0106 / GitHub #364 before BACKEND-DEV implements it. This is the hard gate: implementation must not start until this returns PASS.
acceptance_criteria: Design addresses the diagnosed root_cause in docs/issues/ISS-0106.json (not a superficial workaround like retry/sleep)
All structural changes are documented precisely enough for BACKEND-DEV to implement without ambiguity (which Step objects, which dependency edges)
No implementation code is present in the design (no literal build.zig diff, no Zig function bodies)
Fix scope <= 5 files, matches files_to_change in ISS-0106.json
Classification per templates/lego-catalog.md is correct for this kind of fix (Type E prose, build-graph/test-infra change)

result.summary: src/design/fix-ISS-0106.md independently verified against ISS-0106.json and the live build.zig. Design addresses the ISSUE-FIXER-diagnosed root cause directly (removes the actual dependency-graph concurrency window that lets ISS-503's un-advisory-locked, long-held AccessExclusiveLock DDL transaction race db_integration_test.zig and ~19 other siblings) rather than masking the symptom -- it explicitly rejects retry/sleep/lock-timeout workarounds in both the Summary and the 'Non-goals' section. Structural changes (remove the sibling dependOn edge at build.zig:1258, introduce one new barrier Step aggregating the other ~19+ existing sibling edges, chain run_iss503_integration_tests.step behind that barrier, then re-attach it to test_integration_step) are specified precisely enough to implement without ambiguity, including an ASCII DAG diagram; the one open item (exact barrier-step identifier) is correctly scoped as non-blocking implementation-detail naming, not a design gap. No implementation code present: the only fenced block is an 18-line ASCII diagram, not a literal build.zig diff or Zig function body; confirmed by both manual inspection and tools/lint_design_artefact.py (exit 0, 'OK -- 1 file(s) checked, no issues.'). Error taxonomy explicitly stated as 'None' with justification (pure build-graph/ordering change). Callers/scripts impacted section lists zig build test-integration (behavior change: slight wall-clock increase, justified), zig build test-integration-iss503 (unaffected), and two .github/ files -- both verified to exist on disk; the claim that no .github/workflows directory exists was independently verified (ls confirms it is absent). Fix scope is exactly 2 files (build.zig, tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig), matching ISS-0106.json's files_to_change exactly; the second file's change is explicitly scoped as a doc-comment-only addition (Part 2 advisory-lock hardening explicitly DEFERRED with documented rationale), which is itself a reasonable, well-justified minimality decision rather than scope creep. Type E classification confirmed correct per templates/lego-catalog.md: a build-graph/test-infrastructure ordering change matches none of Type A (CRUD endpoint), B (list page), C (migration), or D (React Flow node) -- Type E is correct by the catalog's own 'when in doubt, prefer Type E' rule, and this is not a doubt case at all. Independent fact-check against live build.zig: every specific line-number and structural claim verified exact -- iss503_integration_tests/run_iss503_integration_tests declared at lines 1106-1116 (design says 1106-1116, confirmed), sibling edge at line 1258 (confirmed, exact text match), narrow test-integration-iss503 step at lines 1303-1305 depending only on clean_test_db.step + run_iss503_integration_tests.step with no sibling edges (confirmed, correctly identified as already-isolated and correctly left untouched), test_integration_step's flat sibling dependOn list spans lines 1245-1266 (22 dependOn calls, confirmed by direct grep) plus exactly two later-appended edges at lines 1396 and 1446 (confirmed by direct grep, no other test_integration_step.dependOn calls exist anywhere else in the file). tools/lint_design_artefact.py does support Type E markdown natively (documented in its own docstring) and was run per the handoff's fn:lint-design-artefact function -- no need to skip it. python tools/codegen_<type>.py --dry-run does not apply since this design produces no templates/specs/*.yaml Type A-D artefact -- correctly out of scope, noted per instructions.

issues.description: The barrier-step naming and whether it must be registered via b.step() to exist as a valid *Step handle is left as an explicit open question for BACKEND-DEV. This is reasonable (it is a non-functional identifier choice with no behavioral impact), but BACKEND-DEV should confirm which construction path this repo's Zig version actually requires before implementing, per the design's own 'Naming guidance' fallback note.

The design's 'Callers/scripts impacted' section reasons about CI timeout impact only in the hypothetical ('If CI is added later...'); since no .github/workflows exists this is correctly out of scope, but worth BACKEND-DEV double-checking no other automation (e.g. a scheduled task or pre-commit hook) invokes zig build test-integration with an assumed duration bound before merging, since the design's own search was limited to .github/.
